title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors — worked eigenvector problems
summary: Three class problems on finding eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors. All three are now fully solved in dropdowns and independently verified; where the notebook contains a slip or stops mid-solution, that is stated explicitly.
transcription_policy: Notebook order and mathematical intent are preserved, with grammar lightly cleaned. Each class problem is presented as a dropdown with a complete independently verified solution. Notebook slips are flagged explicitly rather than silently corrected; material completed beyond the photographed notes is labelled as an independent completion.

math_mismatch.label: Notebook mismatch
math_mismatch.message: In the handwritten final summary for \(\lambda=3\), the third entry of the eigenvector appears without the minus sign. Direct substitution shows that \([2,1,2]^T\) is not an eigenvector for \(\lambda=3\); the verified vector is \([2,1,-2]^T\) (or any non-zero scalar multiple).

source_notes: The source consists of seven notebook photographs: Mac-class-unit2 - 5.jpg through Mac-class-unit2 - 11.jpg; raw notebook images are not copied into website assets.
The top of page 5 is the tail end of the 8 September property example. The dated 9 September work begins at Example 3 below the written date, so only Examples 3–5 are included here.
All three 9 September class questions are now presented as complete dropdown solutions.

Example 3 was independently verified: eigenvalues are 0, 3 and 15. The notebook's final eigenvector for lambda=3 appears to omit the minus sign on the third component; the verified vector is [2,1,-2]^T.
Example 4 contains a notebook slip: the characteristic polynomial factors as -(lambda-8)(lambda-2)^2, so the roots are 8,2,2 rather than 8,6,2. The lambda=2 eigenspace is two-dimensional.

Example 5 is incomplete in the notebook and its determinant setup omits -lambda from the top-left diagonal entry. The dropdown gives the corrected setup and then an explicitly identified independent completion, yielding eigenvalues -3 and 1±2sqrt(2)i.
